chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fadala, from Isma'il ibn Abi Ziyad, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'No servant appoints a deputy over his family with a more superior deputyship than two rak'ahs which he prays when he intends to travel, and says: O Allah, I entrust to You my self, my family, my wealth, my religion, my worldly life, my hereafter, my trust, and the conclusion of my deeds, so He gives him what he asked for.'

key_terms.اسْتَوْدِعُكَ: I entrust to You (form of depositing something valuable with a trustworthy party)
key_terms.بِخِلاَفَةٍ: With a deputyship/representation (metaphor for appointing Allah as guardian)

ai.seo_question: What is the recommended prayer and supplication for a Muslim before traveling?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* under the chapter of the Traveler’s Prayer, this hadith establishes the two-rak'ah *Salat al-Musafir* as a vital spiritual protocol for entrusting one’s soul, family, and wealth to Allah. The specific supplication highlights the comprehensive nature of divine guardianship (*istiwda'*) over both worldly and religious affairs, reinforcing the Shia emphasis on integrating ritual prayer with daily life transitions. This practice serves as a tangible manifestation of reliance on God during the uncertainties of travel.
